The provided text contains several strong indicators of a phishing attempt. First, the message creates a sense of urgency and curiosity by claiming a parcel is waiting, which is a common social engineering tactic. Second, the link "express-delivery-notice.com" is suspicious; legitimate delivery companies typically use their own verified domain names (such as ups.com or fedex.com) rather than generic or misspelled domains. Third, and most critically, the request to enter "home address and payment details" for a redelivery fee is a major red flag. Reputable courier services do not ask for sensitive financial information or payment via unsecured links in unsolicited emails or messages.
